title: Enable CUDA Graph capture/replay with adaptive shape guards and warmup mitigation
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: reduce token-level latency variance and CPU overhead for steady-state inference by leveraging CUDA graph capture/replay while avoiding correctness/perf regressions observed on variable-shape workloads. This PR adds an opt-in CUDAGraphRunner with replay support, conservative shape-guarding heuristics, targeted warmup sequences, and runtime feature flags to enable gradual rollout.

Summary of changes: consolidated the graph capture/replay plumbing into serving/runtime/cuda_graph_runner.{cc,h}, added shape guard metadata tracking to serving/runtime/request_shaper.{cc,h}, modified scheduler to insert warmup requests for newly-captured graphs (serving/scheduler/warmup_manager.{cc,h}), and extended KV cache interaction to mark graphs as non-capturable when cache aliasing is detected (serving/kv/cache_guard.{cc,h}). Added feature flag infra (platform/flags/feature_flags.cc) and a detailed e2e perf test harness (tests/perf/cudagraph_replay_endtoend_test.py).

Behavior and heuristics: capture only when the observed batch size, sequence length distribution and KV cache state are stable for N consecutive requests (configurable via feature flag). Shape guards are implemented as lightweight checks emitted alongside a captured graph; when a guard fails the runner falls back to the interpreter path and triggers a background recapture attempt with updated shape profile. Warmup mitigation: newly-captured graphs are first executed with a configurable warmup token sequence that exercises KV-cache hot paths to avoid first-predictable-token latency spikes.

Regression handling: upstream experiments found a ~4-8% end-to-end regression on workloads with frequent micro-batching and aggressive KV eviction. To address that, this PR introduces a conservative default policy (capture_threshold=20 stable requests) and a telemetry-driven automatic backoff. The PR also includes a diagnostic flag to forcibly disable capture for specific model tags.

Testing and benchmarks: included unit tests for guard logic and integration tests that validate correctness against the interpreter on randomized shapes. Perf numbers (internal): on long-lived chat traffic (median seq_len 512, stable batches=64) we see 12-18% lower p50 token latency and 28% lower p99 compared to interpreter path; on highly variable synthetic workloads the conservative defaults avoid regressions. See tests/perf/README.md for how to reproduce locally.

Rollout plan: feature gated (platform flag "cuda_graph_replay"), staged Canary rollout in Dedicated, telemetry collection for graph hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 deltas, and KV-guard trips. Default remains disabled for Hosted until 95% of canaries report neutral-or-positive latency deltas.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps kernel selection unchanged; subsequent PR will add graph-aware kernel tuning. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes.

Related Linear: ENG-8123, ENG-8279.

merge_commit_message:
Enable CUDA graph capture/replay with adaptive shape guards and warmup mitigation

Consolidated runner, shape guards, KV cache guard, warmup manager, feature flags, and tests.

See ENG-8123, ENG-8279.
release_notes: Added opt-in CUDA graph capture/replay for serving runtime with shape guards and warmup mitigation. Feature is behind the 'cuda_graph_replay' flag and is disabled by default. Admins may tune capture thresholds and KV guard behavior via feature flags. Monitor cudagraph.hit_rate and cudagraph.guard_fail_count metrics during rollout.
notes_for_backport: If backporting to release/* branches: include platform/flags changes and disable feature flag by default. Skip heavy perf tests in older toolchains that lack the capture reliability fixes.
